summary.headline: Sula Q2 FY27 net profit rose 34% YoY to INR8 crore on 4% revenue growth to INR136 crore, with EBITDA margin up 85 bps to 20.3%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 4% YoY to INR136 crore and EBITDA rose 8% to INR27.5 crore, with margin up 85 bps to 20.3%. Net profit grew 34% to INR8 crore, helped by lower interest costs, and net debt fell INR49 crore YoY to INR306 crore. Gross margin fell 280 bps because of higher blended grape costs (about 150 bps impact) and adverse market mix from Telangana. Management expects grape costs to ease from Q4 FY27 as harvest 2027 normalises procurement, though Q3 will still carry the cost.

financial_highlights.value: Down 280 bps YoY (exact level not stated)
financial_highlights.change: Hit by ~150 bps from blended grape cost
Down INR49 crore YoY from INR355 crore (-14%)

financial_highlights.metric: Cash generated from operations after working capital

financial_highlights.value: INR88 crore at Sept 2026 (about INR85 crore after Nov payout of INR4.2 crore)

segments.name: Own brands - elite and premium
segments.commentary: Grew 9% YoY and reached a record 82% of own-brand mix (+420 bps). The Source grew over 30% and crossed 10% of own-brand sales; Sula Merlot grew over 100% and is about 5% of own-brand sales; sparkling wines grew double digits.

segments.name: Own brands - popular and economy
segments.commentary: Under pressure from unsustainable discounting; management says it is maintaining pricing discipline and prioritising profitable sales. Run-rate of about INR23-24 crore was cited by an analyst. Management plans an RTD launch in early December.

segments.name: Wine tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue up 24% YoY to INR16.3 crore, about 20% of total revenue including D2C sales. Room revenue rose 32% (ARR +3%) with The Haven; D2C bottle-shop sales rose 7% to INR9.8 crore; visitor footfalls rose 7%.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Telangana grew nearly 40% and overtook Karnataka as second-largest elite and premium market. Maharashtra improved vs Q1. Karnataka remained subdued due to beer-favouring excise changes. Goa, Rajasthan, West Bengal and exports grew.

guidance_outlook: Grape cost pressure to persist in Q3 FY27; expected to moderate progressively from Q4 FY27 as procurement normalises with harvest 2027 (20-25% table grapes restored, Jan-Mar 2027 harvest).
Management expects gross margin to improve from Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; FY27 closes with controlled wine inventory, benefiting FY28 gross margin.
Immediate EBITDA margin goal of 22-23% over the next couple of years; management called a return to 30% 'far-fetched' for now.
WIPS grant expected at INR49-50 crore for full FY27 vs INR19 crore in H1 (about INR31 crore in H2); last year accrued about INR45 crore.
Goal to improve EBITDA YoY every quarter for the next year.
Maharashtra super distribution in-house, expected to save INR1 crore annually from Q4 FY27.
Fourth hotel (35 keys, York Estate, about INR25 crore investment) targeted for Q4 2028; room count to rise about 20% to 185-190.
capex_capacity: Vintage Room event pavilion at Nashik mother campus is operational (5,000 sq ft, about 300 guests); first event held; incremental revenue expected in H2 FY27 and FY28.

Fourth hotel: 35-key property at York Estate, about INR25 crore investment, payback 5-6 years. Winery operations relocating from York to Domaine Rasa (ex-Chandon estate) by end-Q3 FY27; construction to start in Q4, repurposing the winery building.
Solar supplies 97% of winery energy and 80% of overall energy in H1 FY27.
Battery energy storage to double from 2 MW to 4 MW in coming months.
Maharashtra super distribution logistics to be moved in-house at Domaine Dindori facility.
demand_pricing: Grape procurement mix in harvest 2026 skewed to wine grapes; table grape prices rose from INR15-20/kg to about INR30/kg, so the company stopped sourcing table grapes to cut carryover wine inventory. Wine inventory is down about 80 days from Q2 FY26 to Q2 FY27.
Raw material cost rose about 13% YoY against own-brand growth of about 3.5% in Q2.
Packaging costs (glass, fuel, oil) rose due to Middle East-related disruptions; management does not expect a big further rise.

Management says it holds about 70-75% of the Indian wine market; estimated total elite and premium market (domestic plus imported) at about INR1,000 crore. EU FTA duty cut on wines above EUR2.50 CIF now expected around May 2027 (earlier December-January).
Haryana policy allows imported wines in a retailer quota that Indian wines are excluded from; company is lobbying. Goa showing double-digit growth.
Telangana elite and premium is over 80% red wine and Sula holds over 70% share there.

qa_highlights.question: How will Maharashtra drought affect margins and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this year's dry conditions point to a bumper grape harvest and falling table grape prices, which should cut raw-material costs for economy and popular wines. Premium wines are contracted, so prices stay stable. Irrigation controls could affect the following year's harvest from around April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are the size and growth outlook for India's elite and premium wine market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a total market of about INR1,000 crore including imports, with Sula at 70-75% of the Indian premium segment. It expects growth to be supported by the EU FTA duty cut, though timing has slipped to around May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Was Telangana growth organic after adjusting for base effects, and how do Maharashtra and Karnataka look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Telangana has grown consistently over 5-6 years and Sula has over 70% share in elite and premium there. Maharashtra shows low single-digit growth (high single-digit in premium). Karnataka remains a struggle, and the prior-year destocking will give only a short-term benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the gross margin decline and what can reverse it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gross margin fall was driven by the grape mix, aged inventory overheads and adverse mix. Raw material inflation should ease from Q4 FY27 as inventory is reduced; packaging pressure has eased.

qa_highlights.question: How is WIPS expected to trend in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The company received INR19 crore in H1 and expects INR49-50 crore for the full year, implying about INR31 crore in H2 because 60% of revenue is accrued in H2. The eligibility cap is INR80 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company demerge wine tourism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the topic is under consideration and discussion, but there is no compelling reason to act now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin path after gross margin normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for 22-23% EBITDA margin over the next couple of years and sees positive operating leverage once raw material costs settle. A return to 30% was called far-fetched for now.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on harvest 2027 grape procurement and on wine inventory staying controlled; Q3 FY27 will still carry higher grape costs.
Karnataka (second-largest state historically) remains weak due to excise policy favouring beer; Delhi and Haryana remain difficult.
Popular and economy segment remains under discounting pressure; RTD launch is untested in a competitive category.
Declining monsoon trend and possible irrigation controls from April 2027 could affect future grape supply.
EU FTA timing has slipped to around May 2027.
Management did not say whether the wine tourism demerger is planned.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the premium portfolio, wine tourism and cost actions, and cautious on the gross margin, which management says will stay under pressure through Q3 FY27. Management was evasive on the wine tourism demerger and on any margin target beyond 22-23%.
key_quotes: Importantly, this marks the first quarter in nearly two years in which we have delivered such strong year-on-year earnings growth, and I do believe that this is a positive development for our profitability trajectory.
This is one-time excess inventory correction exercise that has been undertaken.
Our immediate goal would be to at least to go to 22%-23% over the next couple of years.
Telangana has now overtaken Karnataka to become our second-largest market in the elite and premium segment.

adds.what: Fourth hotel, 35-key property at York Estate (~INR25 crore investment)
Vintage Room event pavilion at Nashik (5,000 sq ft, ~300 guests)
Battery energy storage doubling from 2 MW to 4 MW

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; management guides EBITDA margin to 22-23% over two years and gross margin improvement from Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28 as grape costs ease, backed by cost and mix levers and a few small capacity additions (wine-tourism hotel, pavilion) with the winery relocation and fourth hotel not due until later.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects gross margin to improve from Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 as grape costs ease, with EBITDA margin (20.3% in Q2) targeted at 22-23% over the next couple of years, though Q3 FY27 still carries higher grape costs and gross margin fell 280 bps YoY.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vintage Room pavilion is already commissioned and the battery storage doubling (2 MW to 4 MW) is planned in coming months, but the 35-key fourth hotel is not due until Q4 2028 and the winery move to Domaine Rasa only starts construction in Q4 FY27, so the capacity adds are small.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Elite and premium own brands grew 9% YoY (82% of own-brand mix) and Telangana grew nearly 40%, but popular/economy faces discounting pressure, Karnataka remains subdued and total revenue grew only 4% YoY to INR136 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fourth hotel (~INR25 crore) and winery relocation are already committed, and battery storage is being expanded, but no new plant or major capex has been guided and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or volume guidance was given, and management described gross margin as under pressure through Q3 FY27, so an upgrade in the window looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin will stay under pressure in Q3 FY27 from higher grape costs (about 150 bps drag), Karnataka is weak, and EU FTA duty-cut timing has slipped to around May 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans an RTD launch in early December, and The Source and Sula Merlot are growing (+30% and +100% respectively), though the RTD launch is untested in a competitive category.

rows.label: Grape cost easing and inventory reduction
rows.why: Harvest 2027 normalises procurement and wine inventory is down about 80 days YoY, which management expects to restore gross margin after the ~150 bps grape-cost drag in Q2.

rows.label: WIPS grant step-up in H2
rows.why: WIPS grant expected at INR49-50 crore for FY27 vs INR19 crore in H1, implying about INR31 crore in H2 (60% of revenue accrued in H2).

rows.label: Net debt reduction and lower borrowing cost
rows.why: Net debt fell INR49 crore YoY to INR306 crore (-14%) and average cost of borrowing dropped 30 bps to 7.3%, lifting net profit 34% to INR8 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on premium wines, wine tourism and cost actions but cautious that gross margin stays under pressure through Q3 FY27, and evasive on the wine tourism demerger and any margin target beyond 22-23%; analysts probed Maharashtra drought effects, Telangana base effects and the gros
